prompt: What is the key idea of the Merrifield solid-phase method of peptide synthesis?

choices.text: The growing peptide chain is covalently bonded to small beads of a polymer resin, rather than being made in solution
The peptide is made in solution, and each intermediate is crystallized before the next coupling
choices.why: Solid-phase synthesis avoids isolating intermediates: the peptide stays bonded to the resin until the final step.

choices.text: Amino acids are added one at a time to the N-terminal residue, which is attached to the resin
choices.why: The C-terminal amino acid is attached to the resin first, and the chain grows from there.

choices.text: No protecting groups are needed because the resin blocks unwanted reactions
choices.why: Protecting groups are still used; for example, the first amino acid is Boc-protected, and Fmoc is used with the Wang resin.

explanation: In the Merrifield solid-phase method, introduced by R. Bruce Merrifield (1984 Nobel Prize in Chemistry), peptide synthesis is carried out with the growing amino acid chain covalently bonded to small beads of a polymer resin, rather than in solution.

prompt: What resin was used in Merrifield's original procedure?

choices.text: Polystyrene with a –CH2Cl group on about one in every hundred benzene rings
Polystyrene with a –CH2Cl group on every one of its benzene rings
choices.why: Only one of every hundred or so benzene rings carries a –CH2Cl group.

choices.text: The Wang resin, used with Fmoc-protected amino acids
choices.why: The Wang resin with Fmoc is a later, now common improvement, not the original procedure.

choices.text: The PAM (phenylacetamidomethyl) resin, used with Boc
choices.why: The PAM resin, used with Boc protection, is a later and less common variation.

explanation: In the original procedure, polystyrene resin was used, prepared so that one of every hundred or so benzene rings contained a chloromethyl (–CH2Cl) group.

prompt: How is the first amino acid attached to the chloromethylated polystyrene resin in Merrifield's original method?

choices.text: A Boc-protected C-terminal amino acid is attached through an ester bond formed by S_N2 reaction
A Boc-protected N-terminal amino acid is attached through an amide bond formed with DCC
choices.why: The first amino acid attached is the C-terminal one, joined by an ester bond made in an S_N2 reaction.

choices.text: An unprotected amino acid is attached through a disulfide bond
choices.why: The attachment is an ester bond, and the amino acid is Boc-protected.

choices.text: A Boc-protected C-terminal amino acid is attached through an amide bond to the benzene ring
choices.why: The carboxylate displaces chloride from the –CH2Cl group in an S_N2 reaction, forming an ester.

explanation: A Boc-protected C-terminal amino acid is attached to the resin through an ester bond formed by S_N2 reaction with the –CH2Cl group. With the first amino acid bonded, a repeating series of steps builds the peptide.

prompt: In current practice, which resin and N-protecting group are commonly used for solid-phase peptide synthesis?

choices.text: The Wang resin with the Fmoc protecting group
The Wang resin with the Boc protecting group
choices.why: The book pairs the Wang resin with Fmoc; Boc is used with the less common PAM resin.

choices.text: The PAM resin with the Fmoc protecting group
choices.why: The PAM resin is less common and is used with Boc as the N-protecting group.

choices.text: Unmodified polystyrene with no protecting group
choices.why: Protecting groups are always used, and the resin must carry a group that the first amino acid can bond to.

explanation: The steps have been improved over the years. A common procedure uses the Wang resin, developed by Su-Sun Wang, with the Fmoc protecting group. Less common is the PAM (phenylacetamidomethyl) resin with Boc as the N-protecting group.

prompt: Why are mechanical losses minimized in automated solid-phase peptide synthesis?

choices.text: The intermediates stay on the insoluble polymer until the final step
Each intermediate is purified by crystallization before the next step
choices.why: There is no separate purification of intermediates; they stay on the polymer and are simply washed.

choices.text: The peptide chain is synthesized in solution, where nothing is lost
choices.why: In the solid-phase method the chain is bonded to an insoluble resin, not free in solution.

choices.text: Only one amino acid is coupled in the whole synthesis
choices.why: Robotic synthesizers repeat the coupling, washing, and deprotection steps for each amino acid.

explanation: Robotic synthesizers automatically repeat the coupling, washing, and deprotection steps. Each step occurs in high yield, and mechanical losses are minimized because the peptide intermediates stay on the insoluble polymer until the final step. Peptides with 20 amino acids can be routinely prepared in a few hours.
